fix: The official C key for 9701_w21_11_q5 is chemically correct: a metal cation attracts the partially negative oxygen end of water. However, naming ion-dipole interactions is not in the supplied chapter outcomes; KC 9701-3.6.2 tests bond polarity and molecular dipole moments. 1 ammonia
2 hydrogen sulfide
3 boron trifluoride", "options": {"A": "1, 2 and 3 are correct", "B": "1 and 2 only are correct", "C": "2 and 3 only are correct", "D": "1 only is correct"}, "answer": "B", "image": "Assets/mcq/9701_w19_12_q31.png", "marks": 1, "explanation": "B: 1 and 2 only. Ammonia is trigonal pyramidal and hydrogen sulfide is bent; their bond dipoles do not cancel, so both molecules are polar. Boron trifluoride is trigonal planar with three identical B-F bonds whose dipoles cancel.
